summary: Retest #5 of Log-a-Fault multi-photo/video upload. The 600ms-window suppress wrapper in lib/useBackGestureClose path partially works — the FIRST and IMMEDIATE uploads no longer close the dialog (PATH C #1-3 and PATH A #1-2 stay open with chips correctly growing 1→2→3 and 1→2, mount_count stays at 1 / 2 respectively). HOWEVER, a delayed popstate fires AFTER the 600ms suppress window expires (race condition reproduced in headless Playwright), and at that point suppressCloseRef.current is already false → backGestureClose() falls through to closeIssueDialog() → the dialog unmounts. Bug is NOT fully resolved.

ui_bugs.issue: Late popstate (fired >600ms after the OS file chooser returns) still closes the Log-a-Fault dialog. The 600ms suppress timer is racy — in headless Chromium, popstate sometimes arrives ~1.1s after set_files / dropzone click, by which time suppressCloseRef has reset to false. Observed in BOTH PATH C (after upload #3) and PATH A (after upload #2, before user chip-remove click). Mount-count tracking confirms the dialog truly unmounts (not just visibility).

integration_issues.issue: Chip-remove ✕ click effectively appears to close the dialog because a late popstate fires around the same time. Cannot verify chip-remove keeps the dialog open until the popstate race is fixed.

action_items: Replace the 600ms timeout-based suppress with a stronger guard that survives the late popstate. Options the prep note already enumerates: (a) keep suppressCloseRef.current = true until the user interacts with the dialog again (next click/keydown inside DialogContent resets it); (b) detach the popstate handler entirely while a file input is focused / while a recent file dialog is in-flight; (c) tag the phantom pushState entry and ignore popstate if document.activeElement is/was the file input.

Recommendation: in FaultDialogs.js, drop the setTimeout(...600) reset and instead reset suppressCloseRef on the NEXT user-initiated event inside the dialog (pointerdown/keydown listener bound for the dialog lifetime). This eliminates the race completely.

Alternative belt-and-braces: in useBackGestureClose.js, when popstate fires while document.activeElement is an input[type='file'] OR within 2s of the last 'change' event on a file input, swallow it (call history.pushState back) instead of calling onClose().
critical_code_review_comments: FaultDialogs.js L383-385: the 600ms reset is a smell — any timer-based race against OS-level events will be flaky cross-browser. Prefer event-based reset.

useBackGestureClose.js still has no opt-out hook. Consider adding an optional 'shouldClose' predicate so consumers can veto popstate-driven closes without wrapping onClose themselves (the FaultDialogs wrapper currently has to know about lib internals).
Repeated pushState on every Dialog open + back() on clean close pollutes history; consider gating it behind navigator.userAgent mobile detection.

success_rate.frontend: ~70% — uploads no longer close the dialog mid-flight, but the dialog STILL closes from a delayed popstate after the suppress window expires.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use mount-count MutationObserver + a popstate console listener to differentiate genuine dialog-unmount from CSS-hidden. PATH C #1 and #2 fired popstate synchronously (within the 1100ms wait) and were suppressed — those work. PATH C #3 fired popstate AFTER the 1100ms wait → not suppressed → dialog closed. The fix must not rely on a fixed timeout.
rca of the issue: Root cause: the suppressCloseRef is reset by a setTimeout(600ms), but the OS file chooser's popstate event is not bounded to 600ms — it can arrive 0.7-2.0s later (verified in headless Chromium, esp. on the 3rd upload). When the late popstate fires, suppressCloseRef.current === false, so backGestureClose() executes closeIssueDialog(). Reproduction: open Log-a-Fault → upload 3 images via dropzone+file_chooser (PATH C) → wait ~1s → dialog unmounts even with no user action. Mitigation: convert the suppress reset from setTimeout to a user-interaction listener, or detach the popstate listener while a file dialog is in-flight.
